slides.texte_overlay:
habits that make you look
ridiculously intelligent
in every conversation
Summarise the other person's point before answering. "So your worry is the cost, right?" It shows you understood, and your reply instantly sounds sharper.
Use concrete examples instead of big words. "Like when Netflix started by mailing DVDs" beats any jargon. Clear examples are what truly smart people use.
Admit uncertainty with precision. "I'm about 70 percent sure on that." Measuring your confidence sounds far more intelligent than pretending to know everything.
Know a little about a lot. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and being able to connect any topic to something interesting makes me look sharp.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Connecting any topic to something interesting makes me look sharp.

slides.texte_overlay: Ask about the reasons behind opinions. "What made you see it that way?" Curiosity about how people think is a hallmark of a genuinely intelligent mind.
Stay calm when you disagree. Raised voices sound like weak arguments. A relaxed "I see it a bit differently" makes your point look much stronger.
Know when to say "that's a great point." Recognising a good idea that isn't yours shows confidence, fairness and a mind that cares more about truth than ego.
